name: Wakanol
description: Wakanol is a multi-mechanism wakefulness compound that combines orexin agonism, adenosine receptor antagonism, and a proprietary SNT-derived neuroplasticity stabilizer to maintain full cognitive function for 68-76 hours without sleep. Unlike older stimulants that simply mask fatigue, Wakanol actively manages neural waste clearance through a synthetic glymphatic acceleration pathway, preventing the cognitive degradation that accumulates with sleep deprivation. The crash is total and unavoidable — a mandatory 18-22 hour sleep event follows termination.
effects: No fatigue accumulation during active period
side_effects: Mandatory crash: 18-22 hours of near-comatose sleep
Crash sleep is dreamless and unrefreshing subjectively
Repeated use cycles damage glymphatic efficiency permanently
duration: 68-76 hours active, followed by mandatory 18-22 hour crash
cultural_context: Wakanol is the drug of deadlines, of desperation, and of people who are paid by the hour and can't afford to sleep. Tier 2 contract workers use it to double their billable hours before a project closes. Fixers use it to stay active during tense multi-day operations. The problem is the crash — 22 hours of unconsciousness in GLMZ is 22 hours of vulnerability, and people have died during their Wakanol crash in places they shouldn't have fallen asleep.
story_hooks: A key contact went into their Wakanol crash at a critical moment — someone knew the timing and used those 20 hours to completely compromise them, their home, and everything in it.

A Tier 2 worker has been running consecutive Wakanol cycles for six months, sleeping only during the mandatory crashes. Their glymphatic system is failing and they're starting to show signs of rapid-onset neurodegeneration — but they can't afford to stop working.
